title: Data privacy terms in plain English
goal: Explain 8 data privacy terms in plain English, one at a time, with a short workplace example for each.

a.explanation: A flashcard deck: one card at a time slides in with a Lucide icon, its lifecycle stage, the term, a plain-English definition and an amber workplace-example box. GSAP builds one paused timeline with a scene per card, so the host can scrub, step between cards with the markers and replay exactly. A progress row of the 8 terms fills as each card plays, and a lifecycle track under the deck shows where the current term belongs, even in A to Z order. The pacing keeps attention on one idea, but learners never see the terms side by side, and at 3.5 seconds per card the whole deck takes about half a minute, which suits a first read better than revision.
caveats: Each card gets 3.5 s of playback, enough for a definition and a short example at normal reading speed; slower readers may still pause, and the full deck takes 28 s.
On a phone the progress row shows card numbers instead of term names.

b.explanation: All eight cards sit in a grid at once, in the chosen order, each with its number, lifecycle stage, definition and optional workplace example. Playback only moves a highlight: the current card turns blue with a NOW tag, earlier cards get a green tick and a thin bar fills across the top. Plain SVG keeps every word crisp and the whole set scannable, which suits revision and comparison. The trade-off is that nothing directs attention, so a first-time learner faces the whole glossary page at once.
caveats: On a phone the cards stack in one scrolling column and playback scrolls to the current card, so the overview is lost on small screens.
On wide screens the grid may shrink to 90% to fit when examples are on.
